answer: Sybil clusters are an ocean of identical droplets: cheap to mint, indistinguishable at the surface. Weight every vertex where identities meet — grade, vote, attestation — by accumulated graded history, not headcount. Rewards pool like nectar high in the network; only identities that climb via continuous epoch work taste it, and weight decays when work stops. Spawning ten thousand droplets earns less than one established node: each fake head must burn real compute every epoch or evaporate.
